rupee.note: USD/INR up means the rupee is falling. A weaker rupee helps dollar earners and hurts import-heavy sectors; it also raises the imported cost of crude.

crude.sensitivity: Rule of thumb: a sustained $10/bbl rise in crude is roughly a $15–18 bn annual headwind for India's oil import bill. Treat this as an estimate, not a forecast.
crude.note: Crude is the fastest transmission channel from a war or Middle East headline into Indian inflation, the rupee and the Nifty.

fed.pricedIn: VIX is not complacent: the market is already charging some event risk. Confirm direction with DXY, US 10Y and USD/INR.

scenarios.label: Cut 25 bps
scenarios.summary: Liquidity-positive if the cut is accompanied by a dovish tone; often partly priced before the meeting.
rows: Softer dollar usually pulls USD/INR lower; importers get relief.
Rate-sensitive banks, realty and autos lead; watch the press conference for sell-the-news.
Lower funding costs and risk-on sentiment help banks, but the move can fade if credit growth guidance is weak.
Lower real yields and a softer dollar are tailwinds.
Demand optimism supports crude; a weaker dollar is also supportive.

scenarios.label: Hold / hawkish pause
scenarios.summary: The statement and dot plot matter more than the decision; volatility can rise into the press conference.
rows: Dollar steadier; rupee tracks oil and portfolio flows.
Index heavyweights may consolidate until the next inflation or payroll print.
No fresh liquidity impulse; relative strength depends on credit growth.
Higher-for-longer real yields can cap gold.
Policy uncertainty keeps a risk premium in the barrel.

scenarios.label: Hike 25 bps
scenarios.summary: A surprise hike is the risk-off case: stronger dollar, weaker rupee and pressure on rate-sensitive sectors.
rows: Higher US yields can pull portfolio flows out of India.
Valuation compression hits long-duration growth and rate-sensitive pockets.
Higher net interest margins help, but credit-cost and mark-to-market worries dominate first.
Higher real yields and a stronger dollar weigh on gold.
Demand concerns can outweigh dollar moves.
